cite: BBC News, 'Rolf Harris indecent assault conviction overturned', 16 Nov 2017; The Guardian, 'Rolf Harris jailed for five years nine months', 4 Jul 2014

fixes.d: Arrested in March 2013 under Operation Yewtree, Harris was found guilty on 30 June 2014 of 12 counts of indecent assault against four girls and young women between 1968 and 1986. He was sentenced to five years nine months. In November 2017 the Court of Appeal quashed one conviction (the alleged assault of an eight-year-old in Portsmouth in 1969) and upheld the other 11. He died on 10 May 2023.

note: Guardian 4 Jul 2014 confirms 12 counts, 4 victims, 5y9m. BBC 16 Nov 2017: the quashed conviction was the one involving the eight-year-old, so 'one aged eight' had to be tied to the quashed count. Guardian 23 May 2023 confirms death 10 May 2023.

cite: BBC News, Gary Glitter recalled to prison, 13 Mar 2023; BBC News, 'Gary Glitter jailed for 16 years', 27 Feb 2015; The Guardian, 'Gary Glitter abuse trial opens', 2 Mar 2006

fixes.d: Convicted in the UK in 1999 of possessing thousands of child abuse images (about 4,000; jailed four months). He was expelled from Cambodia in 2002 amid sex-crime allegations. In March 2006 a Vietnamese court convicted him of obscene acts with two girls aged 10 and 11; he spent about two and a half years in jail there. In February 2015, after Operation Yewtree, he was convicted of attempted rape, four indecent assaults and one count of sex with a girl under 13, against three girls in 1975–1980, and sentenced to 16 years. Released in February 2023, he was recalled to prison in March 2023 for breaching licence conditions.

note: BBC 27 Feb 2015: 16 years, three girls 1975-1980. BBC/Guardian 2023: 1999 four months, Cambodia expulsion 2002 (record said 2002-03), Vietnam March 2006, ~2.5 years served, recall March 2023. Guardian 2006: girls aged 10 and 11 (BBC 2015 says 11 and 12; kept Guardian's trial-time figure).

cite: BBC News, 'Stuart Hall sentenced for indecent assaults', 23 May 2014; BBC News, 'Stuart Hall jail term doubled by Court of Appeal', 26 Jul 2013; The Guardian, 2 May 2013

fixes.d: In May 2013 Hall pleaded guilty to 14 counts of indecent assault on 13 girls aged 9 to 17 between 1967 and 1986; his 15-month sentence was doubled to 30 months by the Court of Appeal as unduly lenient. In May 2014 he admitted one further indecent assault on a 13-year-old girl and was found guilty of another against the same girl, receiving an extra two years six months (five years in total). He was cleared of rape charges.

note: Guardian 2 May 2013: 14 counts, 13 victims aged 9-17, 1968-1986 (BBC: 1967-1985). BBC 26 Jul 2013: 15 months doubled to 30. BBC 23 May 2014: extra 2y6m, one admitted and one by verdict; offences in 1976-1981. No source puts offending to 1991, so y1 changed to 1986.

cite: BBC News, 'Max Clifford jailed for eight years for sex assaults', 2 May 2014; The Guardian, 28 Apr 2014 and 2 Apr 2019

fixes.d: Clifford was convicted in April 2014 of eight counts of indecent assault against four women and girls, the youngest 15, between 1977 and 1984, and jailed for eight years. His challenge to the sentence failed in November 2014. He died in prison custody in December 2017; the Court of Appeal upheld his convictions posthumously in April 2019.

note: Guardian 28 Apr 2014: eight counts, girls as young as 15, 1977-1985; Guardian 2019: four victims 1977-1984, conviction upheld 2 Apr 2019. Record's 1966 start and 'aged 15 to 19' not supported by sources opened; the upper age 19 could not be confirmed so dropped.

cite: The Guardian, 'Huw Edwards given suspended sentence for accessing indecent images of children', 16 Sep 2024; BBC News, 'Huw Edwards admits child abuse image charges', 31 Jul 2024

fixes.d: BBC newsreader Huw Edwards was arrested in November 2023 and pleaded guilty on 31 July 2024 to three counts of making indecent images of children, received via WhatsApp from another man between December 2020 and August 2021 (41 of 377 sexual images sent were indecent images of children). On 16 Sept 2024 he received six months suspended for two years.

note: Guardian 16 Sep 2024: six months suspended two years, 41 of 377, Dec 2020-Aug 2021. BBC 31 Jul 2024: plea, arrested November (exact day 8 Nov not in opened sources, so removed). Legal images continued to April 2022, so y1 set to 2021 for the illegal images.

cite: BBC News, 'Ex-BBC worker Geoffrey Wheeler guilty of indecent assault', 3 Apr 2017; The Independent, 7 Oct 2015

fixes.d: Launched by the Metropolitan Police on 19 Oct 2012 after the Savile revelations, Yewtree had arrested 19 people by October 2015. Those convicted include Paul Gadd (Gary Glitter), Max Clifford, Rolf Harris, former DJ Chris Denning, Dave Lee Travis (one count, involving an adult) and, in April 2017, ex-BBC worker Geoffrey Wheeler, which the BBC called the operation's sixth conviction; Stoke Mandeville doctor Michael Salmon was also convicted in 2015 after a Yewtree investigation. Others were acquitted or never charged, including several well-known names, and must not be described as offenders.

note: Independent 7 Oct 2015: 19th arrest. BBC 3 Apr 2017: Wheeler was sixth conviction after Clifford, Denning, Gadd, Travis, Harris - so Wheeler's conviction was 2017, not by Oct 2015; the record's 'by Oct 2015 seven convicted' was wrong in timing. Salmon's Yewtree link per Independent headline 17 Dec 2013 (not opened in full).
